title: Rounding up your own spending
description: Sweeping the small change from everyday purchases into savings is a painless habit that quietly builds a cushion.

body.heading: How the trick works
paragraphs: Each time you spend, round the amount up to the next whole unit and move the difference into savings. A coffee at 3.60 sends 0.40 to the pot; a shop at 17.25 sends 0.75. No single transfer is noticeable, which is exactly the point.
Some banking apps do this automatically. If yours does not, a weekly manual version works nearly as well: scan the week's spending, round up the total, and move that amount in one go.

body.heading: Why painless works
paragraphs: Saving schemes fail when they hurt. Rounding up succeeds because the amounts sit below the threshold of attention, the same reason loose change disappears unnoticed when it is not gathered.

Over a year of ordinary spending, the gathered change commonly reaches a few hundred in local currency: enough for a modest emergency cushion, a festive-season fund, or the first milestone of a bigger goal.

body.heading: Give the pot a job
paragraphs: Name the destination before you start, even if it is simply the beginnings of a rainy-day fund. Money swept into a pot with a purpose tends to stay there; money swept into nowhere gets swept back.
Check in monthly, enjoy the total, and resist upgrading the rule until it feels effortless. Habits that stay small stay kept, and kept habits are the whole game.

takeaway: Round up each purchase, sweep the change to a named pot, and let money too small to miss become too useful to ignore.
